political mobilization is a social relationship between two types of political actors, individuals and parties, and that this relationship is characterized by the actors' attempt at influencing the existing distribution of social power.
the process of mobilization is changing, and that this process is a central element of the political modernization of Western societies.

the process of mobilization has become more complex and more differentiated, and that the traditional relationship between individuals and political parties has been transformed into a new relationship between citizens, social movements and parties.

the concept of mobilisation is not a mere descriptive term but a heuristic tool which can help us in analysing and understanding the processes of social change.
